TL;DR: The SEC Division of Corporation Finance added questions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 to its crypto-assets FAQ on November 2, 2026. SEC staff positions may be informative without having the legal force of a statute, judicial judgment or final Commission rule.

This distinction is worth making because crypto regulation often arrives in several formats: speeches, staff statements, enforcement actions, proposals and final rules. They have different implications even when the subject is the same. A dated FAQ update merits attention without being promoted into a sweeping legal turning point.

The SEC Division of Corporation Finance added questions 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 to its crypto-assets FAQ on November 2, 2026. The new staff answers address governance through foundations or organisations, what counts as control over participation and the difference between a functional network and a decentralised one. The page expressly says its answers represent staff views, have no legal force and have not been approved or disapproved by the Commission. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

A functioning crypto system can have a native asset that users need for programmatic activity without necessarily being decentralised. Under the staff explanation, decentralisation is a distinct question about whether any party or group holds operational, economic or voting control. A foundation or association involved in broad-based governance is not automatically a controlling central party; the actual powers and decision rules matter. This is a narrower, more useful clarification than saying every governance token has received a new legal classification.

The additions give lawyers and builders more concrete language for evaluating governance arrangements. A protocol may distribute votes widely while retaining privileged access, unilateral upgrade powers or concentrated economic influence. The staff view asks analysts to study those powers rather than rely on the mere existence of a formal foundation. That could influence how firms document their networks, although it does not eliminate case-by-case analysis or statutory legal requirements.

Crypto policy updates arrive as proposals, staff explanations, enforcement cases and final rules. Those documents carry different legal weight even when they use similar language. A careful article tells readers who issued the text, when it was published and whether it changes obligations now. That distinction is especially important for financial firms making compliance decisions.

This development also connects to two subjects our newsroom has been following: DTCC’s tokenization service and settlement controls and financial infrastructure and technology policy coverage. Those background reports help separate established facts from a new, still-developing announcement.

SEC staff positions may be informative without having the legal force of a statute, judicial judgment or final Commission rule. Investors should also resist the leap from regulatory discussion to token-price predictions. A frequently asked questions page is not an approval notice for any specific exchange, security or stablecoin.

Regulation ultimately affects operational choices: where customer assets are held, who can move them, how decisions are recorded and which risks are disclosed. The market can debate policy direction, but firms still need to map any published guidance to existing duties and the specific activity they carry out. General labels rarely answer those questions.

Watch for direct Commission statements, formal rulemaking notices, court decisions and clarifications that identify the affected transactions. Teams reviewing compliance can use the FAQ alongside primary legal sources, while documenting areas where further advice is necessary. Precision about who issued a document is essential to accurate policy reporting.

One caveat: a week leaves room for other news to take over. The worst 24 hours in the sample came after the December 2021 report, a 17.1% drop that came with a weekend leverage flush.

#5330. Solana Microscope Offers Open-Source Monitoring for Complex On-Chain Operations

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

TL;DR: The Solana Foundation has described Microscope, an open-source monitoring approach for teams managing on-chain programmes and infrastructure. An alert is not a transaction blocker.

Operational tooling rarely generates the excitement of a new token launch, yet it can determine whether institutions trust a network enough to hold meaningful value on it. Teams want evidence that they can detect unexpected actions before the problem expands. Monitoring is one part of that process, not a substitute for preventive controls.

The Solana Foundation has described Microscope, an open-source monitoring approach for teams managing on-chain programmes and infrastructure. The toolkit is designed to help operators inspect instructions, transactions and alerts while connecting observations to common monitoring workflows. It is an engineering tool, not an announcement that every Solana application now receives automatic protection against attacks. The dated original disclosure is the starting point for the figures and product scope discussed here.

In a complex blockchain application, important activity can be hidden within technical transaction instructions that a general-purpose dashboard does not explain well. Monitoring tools try to decode those events and route relevant signals to people who can respond. This is useful for treasury movements, contract administration and unusual operational behaviour, but good alerts depend on choosing the right thresholds and maintaining the integrations.

The wider lesson is that on-chain transparency is not the same thing as operational comprehension. Transaction data may be public while a business still struggles to identify why an event matters or who should investigate it. A self-hostable tool can give teams more control over their monitoring stack, provided they manage uptime, access and alert delivery responsibly.

There is a meaningful gap between a fast transaction and a complete financial service. Solana infrastructure can settle digital assets, but an actual payments or securities product must also manage eligibility, legal rights, local currencies and exceptions. The best reporting follows the full workflow rather than assuming the chain’s speed is the entire product.

For additional perspective, it is worth reading our existing reporting on Solana’s Samsung Wallet rollout and user test and the latest Solana developer and payments coverage. They explain related market structure and should not be mistaken for evidence that every new proposal is already live.

An alert is not a transaction blocker. Microscope does not automatically fix a vulnerable programme, reverse an executed transfer or eliminate the need for security audits. False alarms can consume attention, while incomplete alert definitions can miss harmful activity. A monitored environment still requires tested incident procedures and clear accountability.

Distribution can be an advantage for blockchain applications, but the user experience needs to justify a change in behaviour. Developers also need monitoring and controls to support systems that operate continuously. A credible launch is one that describes available features, supported participants and how success will be measured after the initial announcement.

Watch for adoption in real applications, public documentation and integration examples showing how teams respond to alerts. The most useful evidence would involve measured detection speed and fewer unresolved incidents, rather than the number of dashboards deployed. For Solana developers, monitoring belongs alongside code review and permission design as a basic operating requirement.

#5329. HBAR’s 88% Slide Leaves It Ahead of Most 2021 Rivals

Home » Trendsetter News » HBAR’s 88% Slide Leaves It Ahead of Most 2021 Rivals

A larger token supply complicates any recovery, making a return to its former price a much bigger valuation hurdle.

HBAR remains roughly 88% below its record price, yet the analyst in a recent video places it closer to recovery than most of the largest cryptocurrencies from 2021. That comparison is less a sign of strength than a measure of how severely much of that market has fallen.

Using CoinMarketCap’s November 7, 2021 rankings, the analyst selected the 50 largest coins after excluding stablecoins and wrapped assets. In the video’s snapshot, 41 remained at least 80% below their respective highs, with the median decline around 97%.

“It’s not a forecast,” Cheeky Crypto says. The figures describe historical performance, not the likelihood of a recovery.

At the roughly $0.07 price cited in the video, HBAR would need to rise about eightfold to revisit its approximately $0.57 intraday peak. The analyst separates that brief high from its strongest daily close, just above $0.50 on Binance in September 2021.

The proposed recovery levels start at $0.10, about 43% above the video’s reference price. Next comes $0.25, roughly 3.6 times that price, followed by the record itself.

HBAR has already demonstrated that a substantial rally need not restore earlier buyers’ losses.

Its strongest daily close since 2021 was around $0.37 in January 2025, according to the video, still roughly a quarter below its record close despite an approximately tenfold rise from late 2022.

The bigger obstacle is supply. Cheeky Crypto says the amount of HBAR released from treasury has more than tripled since its record, making a return to $0.57 a materially different valuation proposition.

At the supply level cited, that price would imply a market capitalization near $25 billion. Matching HBAR’s historical peak market capitalization would instead require roughly $0.11 to $0.16 per token, depending on the historical supply figures used.

That valuation is not equivalent to cash that must enter the market, a distinction the analyst explicitly makes. But additional token releases could raise the valuation required to regain the old price.

For investors, the useful distinction is between recovering a token price and recovering a network valuation. HBAR’s smaller drawdown relative to many peers does not erase dilution or make its former high an inevitable destination.

#5327. Zcash (ZEC) Co-Founder Issues Warning on AI Security Threat

Zcash co-founder and computer scientist Eli Ben-Sasson has issued a crucial warning about crypto security amid recent hacker attacks on crypto wallets.

In his latest post on X, Ben-Sasson wrote that the crypto industry faces a key threat besides quantum computers. In particular, he pointed to the growing capabilities of AI as a tool for cybersecurity attacks.

The reason is that today, more than ever before, we rely on cryptography.

"Your crypto keys, your online life, any app that holds something important to you — it's all secured by cryptography," he wrote.

According to Ben-Sasson, the growing power of AI tools puts more pressure on wallet cryptography. This threat is more likely to become an issue before quantum computers pose a significant threat.

"This quick rise in cybersecurity attacks is not going to slow down, not with AI becoming so powerful," Ben-Sasson wrote.

The Zcash co-founder also pointed out the need for stronger cryptographic standards. He specifically highlighted hash-based methods such as ZK-STARKs.

The discussion comes weeks after the infamous Binance hack. The incident resulted in around $6.3 billion in losses from the exchange's hot wallets.

Binance temporarily suspended withdrawals while investigating the breach. The exchange has since reported recovering around 95% of the affected assets.

AI hacker attacks have been on the rise in 2026. According to Google Threat Intelligence statistics, the monthly number of disclosed software vulnerabilities has nearly doubled over the past year.

This means that AI has already become a powerful scanner for potential system weaknesses.

For instance, Casa CSO Jameson Lopp pointed out that attackers can already use AI to automate the search for conventional software bugs and weaknesses in wallet firmware.

In other words, the discussion should be focused on more specific security vulnerabilities in existing software rather than a hypothetical future AI threat.

Panama City, November 4, 2026 — Bitbase today launched ORIGIN, the first season of its new Bitbase Points program. Ahead of the launch, the digital asset exchange credited points to eligible users who had been trading on the platform, so their past activity counts from day one. The season runs for 26 weeks, until May 4, 2027, with 1,000,000 points distributed each week.

ORIGIN is also the first part of Bitbase 2.0 to reach users directly. Bitbase unveiled 2.0 on November 2, with an upgraded app and website and a new brand identity built around the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” The idea is that markets will always move, and Bitbase chooses to focus on what lasts for its users. ORIGIN applies the same thinking to participation. Rather than rewarding a single burst of activity, it looks at what users do day after day over six months and credits the contribution they make across that period.

Bitbase built ORIGIN around what users already do on the exchange. Eligible users, new or existing, are enrolled automatically, with no separate registration. Points are allocated daily based on each participant’s contribution, which draws on four sources: trading, assets held on Bitbase, consistent activity and referrals. Because consistency is one of those sources, steady participation adds up over the course of the season.

ORIGIN also rewards users who bring others to Bitbase. A referrer receives an additional 25% of the contribution of each new user they refer directly, while the new user’s own contribution is unaffected.

Starting November 9, participants will also receive a shareable Trading Identity card that reflects their trading habits, with a new card issued every Monday until the season ends.

“Bitbase 2.0 is about focus, and for our users, that means knowing their steady participation is recognized and credited,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “That’s why ORIGIN started by crediting what users had already done with us. It doesn’t ask anyone to trade differently. It simply records the participation that’s already there, every day, for the next six months.”

Users can track their points and rankings in the Bitbase app and on the website. Full details are available at bitbase.com/points.

Bitbase is a digital asset exchange serving individual and institutional users worldwide, with products spanning Spot, Futures, TradFi and Earn. Bitbase aims to give users a stable and straightforward trading experience, in line with its brand statement, “Market Flows. We Focus.” Learn more at bitbase.com.

#5324. Paraguay Bank-Freeze Puts XRP Custody Risk in Focus

Home » Trendsetter News » Paraguay Bank-Freeze Puts XRP Custody Risk in Focus

A mass bank-account freeze in Paraguay have renewed discussion of XRP and self-custody.

More than 3 million people locked out of their bank accounts overnight: that is the claim driving a video by Edo Farina, a popular researcher covering banks and crypto. He alleges that Paraguay’s central bank took control of digital bank Ueno, using the purported disruption to argue for XRP and self-custody.

Edo Farina’s central comparison is between allegedly inaccessible bank deposits and the XRP Ledger continuing to process transactions. “The XRP Ledger kept settling transactions every few seconds like any other day,” he says.

That distinction concerns network availability, not investment performance. In the same video, he puts XRP near $1.25, down roughly 5%, and bitcoin below $77,000, also falling nearly 5%. These are figures quoted during the recording, not current market prices.

He identifies $1.60 as XRP’s key resistance level and says he would not call a reversal before it is reclaimed.

His broader argument that banking failures will increase demand for XRP as a settlement asset is a forecast; continued ledger operation alone does not demonstrate increased adoption or demand.

The YouTube video’s practical emphasis is on spreading exposure across banks, keeping emergency cash and holding cryptocurrency keys outside exchanges. Exchange-held assets can become inaccessible through platform restrictions, insolvency proceedings or legal action.

But Edo overstates the protection when he says nobody can seize XRP held with personal keys. Native XRP has no issuer clawback mechanism; the ledger does support clawback for certain issued tokens. Neither distinction makes an owner immune to legal orders, stolen keys or compelled transfers.

His claim that physical property cannot be confiscated is similarly too broad. Gold and real estate remain subject to seizure under applicable law.

Holding keys removes reliance on an exchange to authorize transfers, but it does not protect XRP’s market value or make an unverified banking story evidence of its future demand.

On November 2, the exchange introduced Bitbase 2.0, updating its brand, app and website under the statement “Market Flows. We Focus.” ORIGIN is the first program to put that statement into practice. While markets move continuously, Bitbase has chosen to assess participation across months rather than individual moments.

“We designed ORIGIN for users who participate consistently, not only during the busiest periods in the market,” said Nicholas Lo, Chief Business Officer at Bitbase. “Over a six-month season, that consistency carries weight. Our responsibility is to make sure every contribution is credited, from the first day of the season to the last.”

Points and rankings are available in the Bitbase app and at bitbase.com/points.

Bitbase is a digital asset exchange serving individual and institutional users worldwide, with products spanning Spot, Futures, TradFi and Earn. Bitbase aims to give users a stable and straightforward trading experience, in line with its brand statement, “Market Flows. We Focus.” Learn more at bitbase.com.

#5322. Tether CEO Reacts to Massive USDT Demand in Paraguay

Tether CEO Paolo Ardoino has responded to claims that the company's stablecoin, USDT, is being increasingly sought after in Paraguay following a significant banking crisis that cut off millions of people from their savings. Ardinoino has described this as "a flight to safety."

As noted in a recent X post by Bitcoin proponent Samson Mow, Tether's USDT has seen a significant rise in value relative to the Paraguayan guaraní amid the collapse of Ueno Bank, one of Paraguay's biggest digital lenders.

Ueno Bank, with an estimated 3 million customers (a significant percentage of adult Paraguayans), has been hit by a major financial crisis.

According to Mow, USDT has risen from 5,692 guaraníes to over 6,000 guaraníes, an increase of over 5%.

The surge in interest in the U.S. dollar-backed stablecoin USDT, Mow argues, is due to people trying to safeguard their savings outside of the traditional banking system.

USDT's exchange rate rose from about 5,692 guaraníes on Oct. 15 to over 6,000 on Nov. 4.

It is worth noting that even the traditional U.S. dollar rose against the guaraní over the same period.

The rising interest in USDT comes as Paraguay faces a major financial crisis over the collapse of Ueno Bank.

On Nov. 3, Paraguay's central bank announced the start of resolution proceedings for the financial institution after discovering that Ueno Bank's solvency ratio had dropped below half the minimum limit.

The move essentially shut down Ueno Bank, cutting off millions of customers' access to their savings and standard banking services for the time being.

The crisis has also cast doubt on public funds parked at Ueno Bank, including hundreds of millions of dollars from Paraguay's social security system.

The scandal has reportedly already led to the arrest of eight people connected to the bank as well as the resignation of central bank president Carlos Carvallo, as reported by Reuters.

Paraguay's central bank has been trying to reassure depositors, stressing that the situation pertains specifically to Ueno Bank and is not indicative of the collapse of the country's banking system.

Customers with frozen funds at Ueno Bank cannot necessarily convert their deposits to stablecoins until they are able to access their money again.

The financial and market information provided on U.Today is intended for informational purposes only. U.Today is not liable for any financial losses incurred while trading cryptocurrencies. According to a fresh investigation by Santiment, retail investors, giving in to "fear of missing out" on Hyperliquid (HYPE) price rally on October 30, gave four large wallets a perfect opportunity to fully close their positions, bagging $5 million in profit.

Wall Street legend Stan Druckenmiller's first ever appearance on X (former Twitter) with a post about Hyperliquid and the tokenization of trading was supposed to be a declaration of a new era for the popular DeFi exchange. It turned out to be a "sell the news" signal for HYPE tokens' whales.

The best example of 'cashing out' math was educated by the address "0xa2ce...3126". What was a constant accumulation since the end of May, at the peak of the pump, in the $94–$95 range for HYPE token, became a methodical dump worth exactly $225,000 on the market every five minutes. All this was happening while the crowd bought up on the news. The result is a completely empty wallet and its owner locking in $2,395,168 gains.

This whale was not alone in his approach and as Santiment stresses, citing its own on-chain data, four top players opened short positions simultaneously and are now in profit. The only big buyer who believed in HYPE price growth is losing more than 11%.

The token's price chart against USD only confirms a total exodus of big buyers at the time of writing. The Oct. 30 pump candle left a huge upper wick with a trace of those very five-minute sales. The HYPE price has already slid more than 12% and is squeezed in the $81.79–$85 range. The local level of $84.150 has been broken from top to bottom, and now the token is slowly drifting to the next strong support at $78.020.

Traditional finance's 'big guns' like Druckenmiller undoubtedly remain the best marketing tool for crypto projects. The only difference is that for retail investors a billionaire’s tweet became a call to action, and for big capital an exit order.

The buyers’ rush created a perfect liquidity window for the whales — a chance to sell off huge volumes of coins without the price slipping down. What this makes of the story is that the technology and business of Hyperliquid turned out not to equal the price of decentralized exchange's native token.

#5318. PEARL integrates with NEAR Intents to expand cross-chain access for AI miners — Can demand follow?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Pearl, the native token of the Pearl Layer-1 network, has launched on NEAR Intents. The move allows for swapping of tokens across more than 35 different networks. Additionally, the integration provides the Near Protocol’s [NEAR] Click API.

As a result, this makes it possible for wallets and applications to integrate Pearl [PEARL] token swaps.

In simple words, through NEAR’s infrastructure, miners will be able to swap PEARL for assets within all of those 35+ networks. Therefore, there may be easier access to stablecoins or other currencies for miners as they pay for electricity and hardware.

More importantly, Pearl’s Proof of Useful Work model links token issuance to AI computations that also secure the network. As such, miners receive both block rewards and inference fees based upon the same workload they are using to mine blocks.

This link could create a direct relationship between AI usage and token utility. However, for PEARL to have sustained value, it will require consistent AI-related workloads creating sufficient activity and generating fees that can support miners.

As part of the integration, NEAR intents provides PEARL with access to an existing cross-chain market. No additional cross-chain bridges for each individual network would be required for this.

Currently, NEAR intents’ ecosystem provides a cross-chain marketplace that includes approximately 38 networks, along with more than 200 assets. Major stablecoin markets are included in the asset list as well.

This is important for miners who need to have liquid means to exit transactions quickly in order to meet costs associated with electricity and hardware. NEAR intents reported more than $37 billion in cumulative volume and more than $144 million in daily volume traded.

A large trading platform like this offers stability for those looking to utilize cross-chain swaps.

Moreover, confidential transactions enable users to transfer funds anonymously. Although the fact that the entire network is utilizing this function does not necessarily mean that there will be a greater demand for PEARL.

Instead, it will rely upon how frequently miners and traders utilize these services to conduct swaps, develop deeper liquidity levels, and ensure reliable execution.

PEARL’s next challenge is converting wider access into sustained market demand. PEARL’s market activity will show whether easier cross-chain access translates into genuine demand. At press time, the token was trading around $1.69, up 17% in the last 24 hours.

The daily volume increased alongside price rally, hovering near $12 million and was up 36%.

However, activity remains concentrated on a few centralized exchanges, suggesting NEAR access has yet to reshape its liquidity. This matters because GPU miners need reliable markets to convert rewards into operating funds.

Ultimately, stronger demand must therefore come from real AI workloads and paid inference, not token issuance alone.

PEARL (PEARL) has joined NEAR Intents, gaining confidential swap access across more than 35 blockchain networks.

PEARL’s long-term demand will depend on real AI workloads, paid inference, and sustained trading activity.

#5317. Gate Pioneers Proof of Security (PoSEC), Achieving 104.58% Cold Storage Coverage to Solidify Asset Security

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Gate has officially introduced Proof of Security (PoSEC), a new asset security verification framework, becoming the first digital asset trading platform in the industry to launch a PoSEC security verification system. Since its founding in 2013, Gate has consistently placed user asset security at the forefront of its priorities. With the introduction of PoSEC, Gate extends security verification beyond reserve adequacy to include asset storage structures and risk coverage capabilities, further solidifying safeguards for user assets and providing a new practical approach to advancing industry security standards.

Unlike Proof of Reserves (PoR), which primarily verifies the adequacy of asset reserves, PoSEC places additional emphasis on asset storage security. By publicly disclosing the distribution of assets between platform cold storage and hot wallets, PoSEC provides visibility into asset storage structures and their ability to cover potential losses under extreme scenarios.

PoSEC introduces the cold storage coverage ratio as a key metric to measure the extent to which cold storage covers total user assets. A coverage ratio ≥ 100% means that, under the applicable calculation methodology, cold storage alone would be sufficient to cover all user assets even if all assets held in hot wallets were lost. PoR and PoSEC serve complementary purposes, extending asset security verification from reserve adequacy to storage security and risk coverage, while providing users with more comprehensive and transparent information about asset security.

According to the snapshot taken at 00:00 (UTC) on November 4, 2026, Gate’s cold storage coverage ratio reached 104.58%, with cold storage and hot wallet assets accounting for 88.26% and 11.74% of total assets, respectively. Cold storage assets include digital assets held offline and traditional assets under independent custody. To qualify, these assets must meet requirements such as not being directly used for routine deposits and withdrawals, being held offline or under independent custody, requiring multi-party authorization for transfers, and being independently verifiable.

The current data is undergoing verification by an independent third-party audit firm. The review covers asset authenticity and control, valuation and calculation methodologies, and coverage ratio calculations. The audit report will be published on Gate’s official website upon completion, enhancing the transparency and credibility of asset security disclosures.

Gate has long been committed to digital asset security and transparency. In 2020, Gate was among the first in the industry to introduce an open-source Proof of Reserves (PoR) mechanism and a Merkle Tree-based asset verification solution, establishing itself as an early contributor to reserve transparency in the industry. Gate subsequently incorporated technologies such as zk-SNARKs to enhance its asset reserve verification framework.

As of October 18, 2026, Gate’s total reserves amounted to approximately $8.688 billion, with an overall reserve ratio of 118.49%. The platform also employs a range of security mechanisms, including hot and cold wallet segregation, multi-signature technology, Multi-Party Computation (MPC), dynamic risk monitoring, and zero-trust access control, to establish a multi-layered security framework covering asset reserves, storage management, and risk protection.

From PoR, which verifies reserve adequacy, to PoSEC, which verifies asset storage security and risk coverage capabilities, Gate is progressively building a multi-layered security framework encompassing asset reserves, storage management, risk protection, and public verification. Looking ahead, Gate will continue to uphold its security-first principle, further develop PoSEC standards and verification mechanisms, and collaborate with more industry participants to enhance asset security and transparency, laying a stronger security foundation for the long-term, sustainable development of the digital asset industry.

Learn more: https://www.gate.com/proof-of-security

Gate, founded in 2013 by Dr. Han, is one of the world’s leading cryptocurrency and integrated financial services platforms, spanning financial and everyday use cases including asset management, trading and payments. Serving over 62 million users globally, it supports trading across 5,400+ digital assets and 12,800+ stock assets and ETFs, while providing access to a comprehensive range of TradFi assets, including metals, stocks, indices, forex, and commodities to meet users’ end-to-end needs across asset holding, trading, and spending. As an industry benchmark, Gate was among the first platforms to implement 100% Proof of Reserves. Its ecosystem includes Gate Money, Gate Wallet, Gate Ventures, Gate for AI Agent, and a wide range of products and services.

Real-world assets value of US investment behemoth Franklin Templeton on Stellar (XLM) chain officially hit a $1.1 billion milestone as net capital inflow into tokenized money market fund BENJI totaled $200 million.

RWA Foundation's report, based on Token Terminal data, now signals an infrastructure-scale gap in the volume of institutional funds between Stellar and XRP Ledger, two blockchain techs that share the same origin thanks to Jed McCaleb. Stellar became for Franklin Templeton the second network in terms of significance after BNB Chain, surpassing even Ethereum.

Almost all RWA liquidity inside Stellar is shared between four of the biggest platforms. The undisputed leader remains Spiko, holding about half of the market there with $2 billion in tokenized funds. Second comes Franklin with its flagship fund, while the BlackRock-backed Ondo and Realiz split the remainder, commanding about half a billion dollars each.

The presence of Franklin Templeton on the XRP Ledger is still limited to just the sgBENJI fund worth $200 million. For Stellar it's not only 10-fold dominance in unique RWA-tokens holders, but also hundreds of millions in monthly volume of asset distribution against just $22 million for XRPL.

Sudden overnight jump worth $200 million by BENJI on Stellar managed to amaze even the market veterans. Representatives of RWA-platform ZeusRWA confirmed that the liquidity injection came at the buzzer:

«Franklin Templeton decided to add another hundred million just as we were about to publish…», researchers noted in comments to the report release.

The most striking demonstration of the gap between Stellar and XRPL is in the stablecoin segment. Amid similar numbers in how many of them are on both of the chains, 'digital dollars' on the XLM-linked chain are more used in commercial payments where their monthly transit volume hit $20.48 billion. On XRPL the same metric is at $9 million, which proves that they are simply held on balance without real usage in the ecosystem's payment tunnels.

The spike in Stellar dynamics in the second half of 2026 is backed by successful integrations inside the industry. Chainlink's price oracle has been locked in, while a key long-term factor is guaranteed by a joint venture with the US central repository DTCC which is expected to be the direct release of traditional financial vehicles into on-chain space by the first half of 2027.

#5315. Polygon eyes hard fork to recover $6.5 mln in stolen POL – But at what cost?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

In a surprising development, Polygon has proposed a major network upgrade to recover approximately 70.49 million POL tokens, worth around $6.5 million. These were those tokens that were stolen during two separate security incidents involving Polymarket and Binance in October 2026.

The proposal aims to move the stolen tokens from five attacker-controlled wallets into recovery wallets designated by the compromised companies.

5 attacker-controlled addresses hold about 70.49M POL: about 23.86M POL (4 addresses) from the Polymarket incident and about 46.63M POL (1 address) from the Binance incident. The funds cannot move, but nothing in the current setup lets them be returned either.

Polygon’s block producers have already added these addresses to their transaction blocklists. This they did to prevent the attackers from moving the funds further. However, this measure only freezes the assets, and it does not return them to their actual owners.

The existing system also requires block producers to restart their infrastructure whenever blocklist changes are made, making it difficult to maintain these restrictions over time.

Hence, to address this issue, Polygon has proposed a hard fork, which is a major network upgrade that changes the blockchain’s underlying rules.

Under the proposal, at a predetermined block, the POL balances of the five identified wallets would be reduced to zero. The same amounts would then be credited to recovery addresses verified and designated by Polymarket and Binance.

However, for this plan to succeed, the proposal also requires both companies to prove ownership of their designated recovery addresses before the upgrade. If approved, developers will first implement and test the changes on Polygon’s Amoy testnet before deploying them on mainnet.

At the same time, validators, exchanges, and node operators will also need to upgrade their software before activation. However, the proposal has raised important questions about decentralization and user ownership.

Normally, blockchain transactions cannot be reversed or wallet balances moved without the owner’s private keys. But Polygon’s proposed intervention would override this principle through a consensus-level change.

It is an extreme action that should not be reproduced commonly.

This comes as the Polygon’s MATIC was trading at $0.098 after a hike of 2.08% in the past 24 hours.

But with 21Shares recently withdrawing approximately $11 million worth of POL from Coinbase over the past 30 days, including 45.7 million POL worth $4.08 million on 28th October, concerns remain.

#5311. US Voters Back AI Data Center Restrictions in At Least 29 Communities

US Voters Back AI Data Center Restrictions in At Least 29 Communities

Voters in at least 29 U.S. jurisdictions backed bans or restrictions on data-center development Tuesday, according to The Washington Post, dealing a new setback to the massive infrastructure buildout behind artificial intelligence.

The measures ranged from outright prohibitions to requirements for additional public approval. Some were nonbinding advisory votes, meaning their passage does not automatically stop construction.

Ballotpedia tracked 41 data-center measures on November 3 ballots across 10 states. Twenty-eight were framed so that a yes vote would curb development, while 13 would permit or support projects, meaning rejecting one of the latter could also count as a defeat for developers.

Ohio produced some of the clearest results. All 10 charter measures backed by the grassroots group Conserve Ohio passed, according to the Post, and more than three-quarters of voters in Hubbard, Ohio, supported a ban on data centers.

The negative sentiment is so big that voters in Granville, Trenton, and Sunbury backed restrictions with margins of roughly 78% to 82%.

In Illinois, nearly 80% of voters in Joliet Township rejected an advisory proposal supporting AI data centers. In Janesville, Wisconsin, more than 60% approved a requirement for another public vote before major development at a former General Motors site linked to a proposed data center.

These facilities house the chips and servers used to train and run AI systems. Their appetite for electricity has turned proposed campuses into local fights over utility bills and grid capacity, while opponents also raise concerns about water use, noise and deals struck without public scrutiny.

AI companies are aware of the growing backlash and are already working to counter it. Some are stepping up lobbying efforts, while others are turning to public relations campaigns to reshape public perception. OpenAI, for instance, has sought to rebrand data centers as “compute campuses,” in an effort to distance the facilities from the negative connotations increasingly associated with them.

The votes arrived alongside victories by politicians promising tougher oversight of data centers. Democrat Gina Hinojosa defeated Republican Gov. Greg Abbott in Texas after campaigning for a moratorium on new projects, while Ohio's governor-elect Amy Acton also supports a pause and stricter rules.

Industry leaders have warned that blanket restrictions would put U.S. AI investment at risk. BlackRock CEO Larry Fink said last month that a broad moratorium could have serious economic consequences. "If we have a moratorium of some sort in this country, we will be in a recession," he said.

#5310. 4 Korean Deals Accelerate Ripple’s Institutional Push

Home » Trendsetter News » 4 Korean Deals Accelerate Ripple’s Institutional Push

South Korean financial institutions have signed agreements with Ripple, testifying to a growing interest in digital-asset custody.

Four South Korean financial institutions have signed agreements with Ripple within six months, according to Kamilah Stevenson, a wealth-focused market commentator tracking the company’s expansion.

Her latest video points to an insurer, an internet bank, a regional lender and a securities firm as evidence of growing institutional interest, but their involvement does not necessarily translate into XRP demand.

The most consequential detail is the emphasis on custody. Three of the four arrangements begin with infrastructure for safeguarding digital assets, rather than cryptocurrency trading or payments.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson says Kyobo Life agreed in April to test holding, transferring and settling tokenized Korean government bonds using Ripple Custody. The stated objective is to shorten settlement from roughly two days to something closer to immediate execution.

K Bank followed at the end of April, selecting Ripple Custody to develop digital-asset wallets for institutional clients, according to the video. A regional bank then adopted Ripple Payments in August for cross-border business transfers.

The fourth agreement involves Meritz Securities, which the commentator describes as Ripple’s first Korean securities-firm partner. Its work will focus on custody and tokenization, with potential interests including spot crypto ETFs, fractional investments, security tokens and won-backed stablecoins.

“Where does it sit and who’s responsible for keeping it safe?” the host asks, arguing that custody approvals lay the groundwork for subsequent products. That is the video’s central thesis: institutional adoption starts with operational controls, not necessarily a tradable token.

Dr. Kamilah Stevenson identifies February 4, 2027, as the effective date for new Korean legislation covering tokenized securities, and cites a November 11 deadline for public comments on proposed rules. Those dates are presented as a potential catalyst, although the transcript does not independently establish the regulatory timetable.

For XRP investors, the distinction between Ripple’s business and XRP usage crucially matters. Ripple Payments can use XRP for currency conversion, but the YouTube video does not establish that the Korean bank’s payment flows actually do.

Sharing a ledger, however, does not mean every exchange between stablecoins must route through XRP. The agreements suggest broader institutional interest in digital-asset infrastructure; their effect on XRP demand will depend on which services reach production and how transactions are settled.

#5308. XRP Ledger Welcomes New Euro Stablecoin

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) community has welcomed a new stablecoin to the blockchain. This time, it's via GateHub, which is launching a new euro-pegged stablecoin for blockchain payments that links the blockchain to the traditional European banking network.

As announced in a press release on Nov. 5, GateHub partnered with Slovenian financial services company Dinaro to launch GateHub Euro (EURGH), a MiCA-compliant (European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation) stablecoin pegged to the euro.

The new stablecoin operates on both the XRP Ledger and Xahau, an alternative blockchain in the larger XRPL ecosystem with smart contract capabilities.

Part of the significance of EURGH is its SEPA (Single Euro Payments Area) integration. With this, GateHub users can make instant euro payments from their XRPL and Xahau wallets to banks in Europe.

GateHub notes that these transactions can take just seconds to complete, linking blockchain assets to the traditional banking world.

GateHub Euro is a stablecoin that is designed to maintain a value of exactly one euro. This means 1 EURGH should equal €1. It is an electronic money token (EMT) under the EU's MiCA regulations.

GateHub Euro is issued by Dinaro, which is an authorized electronic money institution regulated by the Bank of Slovenia.

According to Dinaro's published terms, it will issue EURGH on a 1:1 basis when it receives Euro funds. Holders of the token will be able to redeem EURGH for Euros at face value (subject to proper checks and compliance procedures).

GateHub users can access traditional European payment systems via their digital wallets because of the SEPA integration. This is an alternative to traditional crypto exchanges for converting funds into the traditional banking network.

GateHub Euro is not the first euro-pegged stablecoin to emerge in the crypto space or on the XRP Ledger.

For instance, there's the MiCA-compliant euro stablecoin EURØP from Schuman Financial.

Meanwhile, there's Circle's EURC, which is a euro-pegged stablecoin for payments and trading on multiple blockchains.

And there's EUR CoinVertible (EURCV) from Société Générale-FORGE, a digital asset business unit of French banking giant Société Générale.

#5304. Solana’s Faster Finality Fails to Halt SOL’s Price Slide

Home » Trendsetter News » Solana’s Faster Finality Fails to Halt SOL’s Price Slide

Solana’s Alpenglow upgrade reportedly cut transaction finality to roughly 400 milliseconds, but still can’t pick SOL’s price up.

Solana transactions reportedly reached finality in roughly 400 milliseconds after its Alpenglow upgrade, yet SOL fell after the switch. In the supplied video, a crypto analyst examines that disconnect: a faster network may improve its appeal to payment providers without immediately giving investors a reason to buy.

Fire Hustle places the upgrade’s launch on October 21 and describes SOL trading near $100 afterward. The YouTube video’s central argument is that technical progress remains secondary to broader market conditions and investment flows when it comes to short-term prices.

According to her, Alpenglow replaced Solana’s TowerBFT voting system, moving validator votes off-chain and reducing finality from about 12.8 seconds to roughly 400 milliseconds in the first day’s data. That remains above the team’s stated 150-millisecond target.

The transition required validators representing at least 82% of staked SOL to approve the new system before user transactions resumed. The analyst describes a brief pause rather than a reported outage, following months of test-network rehearsals.

There is also a software-diversity concern. The YouTube video episode says Firedancer validators could not participate in the switch and temporarily had to return to the main client, leaving the network more dependent on one implementation.

Moving votes off-chain also changes the transaction count displayed by block explorers. “Check what’s actually being counted before you panic,” she says, warning that lower headline transactions-per-second figures need not mean user activity has collapsed.

Fire Hustle reports 12 consecutive trading days of outflows from Solana ETFs and describes October as their worst month for withdrawals since launch. It also cites a roughly 12% weekly decline in open leveraged SOL positions on OKX.

Corporate buyers offered a counterpoint. According to Fire Hustle, DeFi Development Corp. purchased another 22,070 SOL during the decline, while Forward Industries added approximately 949,000 SOL in the quarter ending September.

On the chart, she watches support in the mid-$90s and an initial recovery zone around $110–$115. Those are conditional trading levels, not price forecasts: a weekly break below support could expose the $80s.

In a nutshell: faster settlement could support payment adoption, but sustained usage and a reversal in fund outflows would offer firmer evidence that the upgrade is translating into market demand.

#5303. US Bank Regulator Issues First AI Framework as Banks Battle Rogue Agents

US Bank Regulator Issues First AI Framework as Banks Battle Rogue Agents

The U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued its first supervisory framework for artificial intelligence in banking today, telling examiners to focus less on how powerful an AI system is and more on what happens when it makes a mistake.

The OCC's framework addresses that very concern, although the regulator has not linked its issuance to those specific incidents.

In a section covering operational resilience, the agency warns that external agents operated by customers, fintechs, or other businesses could create risks for banks even when the banks don't control those systems.

It suggests examiners consider measures including identity verification, delegated permissions, transaction limits, monitoring, and the ability to suspend or revoke access.

The guidelines aim to tackle the dilemma of how to let customers use AI assistants to manage their finances without giving autonomous software unrestricted access to accounts that banks are already facing.

The new OCC guidance arrives less than two weeks after reports that major banks were discovering unauthorized third-party AI agents operating inside customer accounts, sometimes taking actions that appeared to go beyond users' instructions.

Morgan Stanley was blocking outside agents, while JPMorgan, Bank of America, and Citi were restricting access, according to an Axios report on October 22. Bank executives described the situation as "horrifying," raising questions about who controls an autonomous agent once it has access to someone's money.

The OCC's framework makes a distinction between an AI system's technical sophistication and the damage it could cause.

A simple agent authorized to initiate financial transactions may present greater risk than a more advanced model limited to writing internal documents, the regulator said.

Under the 22-page framework, examiners can consider the consequences of failure, whether an action can be reversed, and how much control humans retain over the system.

The agency outlines four illustrative risk tiers. Fully autonomous payment agents and real-time credit decision systems fall into the highest category, while basic internal productivity tools occupy the lowest.

Higher-risk systems may warrant tighter restrictions on autonomy, independent testing, and human approval before consequential actions can proceed.

The framework also addresses AI systems that continue operating while making harmful decisions. Suggested safeguards include circuit breakers, rate limits, restricted permissions, and emergency shutdown controls.

Those considerations are especially relevant to the outside agents described in Axios's earlier reporting, where banks struggled to distinguish legitimate customer-authorized software from systems operating beyond their intended permissions.

The OCC stressed that the document does not create new regulatory requirements or enforceable standards for banks.

Instead, it gives examiners a way to evaluate AI within existing operational, compliance, and cybersecurity risk categories. Banks are not required to establish a separate AI risk category.

The document uses the mandatory term "Super Intelligence," which the Donald Trump administration insists on using in place of “artificial intelligence,” but its scope includes conventional AI and “autonomous agents” rather than only hypothetical systems with intelligence beyond human capabilities.

The framework covers AI used in payments, fraud detection, customer service, and other banking operations. It also extends its risk considerations to external AI agents connecting through bank channels.

The OCC said it intends to update the guidance as the technology develops. For now, its illustrative risk scale puts autonomous payment agents in the highest-risk category, regardless of how well they perform in testing.

#5301. Crypto Industry Faces New Threat as Warren Eyes Powerful Senate Role

The cryptocurrency industry may face major regulatory hurdles following the Democrats' victory in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections.

Longtime cryptocurrency critic Elizabeth Warren is set to lead one of the Senate's most powerful committees, according to a Nov. 5 report by The Wall Street Journal.

The WSJ report by Corrie Driebusch and Dylan Tokar described Warren's 20-year record of clashing with Wall Street, holding bankers accountable, delving into private equity and examining big financial firms.

Chairing the Senate Banking Committee would also give Warren more power to conduct investigations and issue subpoenas.

The news means greater oversight in Congress and potentially more scrutiny of the cryptocurrency industry, a sector that has often clashed with Warren over financial regulation. It could lead to even more hurdles for industry-friendly laws.

Warren is among the most vocal critics of the cryptocurrency sector in Washington.

Back in March 2023, her reelection campaign famously endorsed her "anti-crypto army" campaign, something cryptocurrency proponents took great offense to.

Warren has often tied cryptocurrency to money laundering, ransomware, sanctions busting, and other financial crimes.

Recently, Warren has opposed Republicans' push for the Digital Asset Market Clarity Act. She says the bill lacks sufficient consumer protections and financial crime safeguards.

In a Sept. 15 Senate speech, she argued that the U.S. should regulate crypto but opposed crypto bills designed to benefit the industry.

Should Warren take over the Banking Committee in January 2027, she will have much more say in which crypto proposals move forward and which industry executives are grilled.

#5299. XRP Ledger's Biggest Lending Upgrade Just Got Closer

The XRP Ledger (XRPL) is on the verge of a significant decentralized finance (DeFi) upgrade that could potentially open up new lending possibilities and liquidity for the XRP Ledger network.

According to Vet (@Vet_X0), a notable XRPL validator and community member, the much-anticipated Lending Protocol amendment has now gained two more Yes votes from validators, moving one step closer to activation.

The Lending Protocol amendment now boasts 21 Yes votes from a total of 35 trusted validators (60%). The amendment needs eight more Yes votes to reach the minimum threshold of 29 validators.

Reaching this threshold doesn’t mean that the upgrade will instantly go live. Instead, reaching the supermajority threshold will initiate the mandatory two-week activation period, which requires a minimum of 80% of validators to support the amendment.

The upgrade, known as XLS-66, is geared towards adding a native lending feature to the XRP Ledger.

In contrast to most crypto lending services, where borrowers are typically required to provide more collateral than the loan amount, XLS-66 is specially crafted to enable fixed-term and non-collateralized lending.

This will enable qualified borrowers to secure loans without the need to hold cryptocurrency collateral that exceeds the loan amount.

According to the official XLS-66 document, the Lending Protocol will enable the pooling of funds via so-called Single Asset Vaults, which can then be loaned to borrowers under set terms.

The proposed lending system involves three key actors: depositors, loan brokers and borrowers.

While depositors are in charge of depositing crypto or supported assets into a vault, loan brokers are tasked with brokering lending deals as well as evaluating borrowers.

For their part, borrowers would receive the loans and pay them back based on the set schedule.

The upgrade could potentially empower financial institutions and other entities to put capital to use on the XRP Ledger, as opposed to just holding or moving around assets.

It may also open up new prospects for earning interest on deposited assets in lending vaults. The amount of interest, however, would largely depend on the actual lending activity and risks.

According to the latest validator data, this amendment has reached 23 out of 35 votes. It still requires six more votes to hit the threshold.

Furthermore, the LendingProtocolV1_1 amendment, which offers upgrades including closed-ended vaults, updated interest accounting, etc., also currently has 21 Yes votes.

All three amendments are currently being considered, and none has yet reached supermajority.

We are nearing full delivery under our first colocation agreement while construction under our second is underway across five campuses.

According to the reports, the company’s colocation revenue surged nearly 60% quarter-over-quarter to $215.4 million, compared to $136.7 million in Q2 2026 and $15 million in Q3 2025.

In fact, its total revenue also increased to $232.9 million, up from $164.2 million in the previous quarter and $81.1 million a year earlier.

As of the 30th of September, Core Scientific was billing for 485 megawatts (MW) of capacity, up from 395 MW in the previous quarter, representing more than $700 million in average annualized colocation revenue.

That said, the company also reported net income of $1.178 billion, compared to a net loss of $1.15 billion in Q2 2026 and $144 million in Q3 2025.

Meanwhile, adjusted EBITDA more than tripled quarter-over-quarter to $133.6 million, with its margin expanding to 57% from 25% in the previous quarter. Core Scientific’s gross profit also climbed to $123.3 million, compared to $70 million in Q2.

However, on the mining side, self-mining revenue declined to $12.3 million from $21.5 million in the previous quarter, while hosted mining revenue stood at $5.17 million. At the same time, revenue from hosting equipment for other Bitcoin miners also declined to $5.2 million from $8.7 million.

For those unaware, Core Scientific began its AI infrastructure transition in 2024 through hosting agreements with CoreWeave, covering 590 MW of capacity, of which 485 MW was billable by September 2026. However, the transition also comes with challenges.

Core Scientific recorded $266.5 million in mining-related asset impairments in Q1 2026 amid weaker Bitcoin prices, low mining profitability, and declining equipment values. It also recorded a $41.9 million loss after terminating mining equipment agreements with Block and Proto in Q2.

That said, Core Scientific is not the only one, as, according to AMBCrypto’s recent report, Bitcoin miners are increasingly selling BTC to fund operations while shifting their infrastructure towards AI and HPC.

This comes as miners swung from a huge inflow spike of about +7K BTC  in early 2026 to an outflow of about -5.7K BTC in early November, while the price slid from around $95K to $75.5K.

However, the latest netflow has settled back to a small positive reading of about 179.4 BTC, which suggests the miner selling pressure has cooled.

#5297. Ethereum software bug triggers emergency fixes across major layer-2 networks

Paradigm says a bug in Reth could produce incorrect blockchain state calculations, prompting coordinated patches across major Ethereum infrastructure.

A software flaw that could allow specially crafted transactions to produce incorrect blockchain state calculations has prompted coordinated fixes across Ethereum infrastructure.

On Nov. 5, Georgios Konstantopoulos, chief technology officer at crypto investment firm Paradigm, said that developers had released patches for Reth, Optimism, Base and Tempo after discovering an error in software used to process blockchain transactions.

The vulnerability affected Reth, an Ethereum execution client developed by Paradigm that provides critical infrastructure for networks operating within the Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) ecosystem.

According to Konstantopoulos, the flaw originated in Reth's legacy state-root calculation system, which could return an incorrect result when processing certain smart contract storage configurations.

A state root is a cryptographic fingerprint representing a blockchain's current state, including account balances and smart contract data. An incorrect calculation can cause nodes to disagree about the validity of a block, potentially disrupting transaction processing or network synchronization.

“Reth's legacy state root code had an edge case,” Konstantopoulos explained, adding that a carefully crafted transaction could trigger the error under specific conditions.

Reth's block-building software used the vulnerable calculation method on lower-end hardware and in networks built with Optimism's OP Stack, extending the potential exposure beyond Ethereum's mainnet infrastructure.

The Tempo development team discovered the issue through automated security testing. The testing technique, known as fuzzing, involves feeding software unusual or unexpected inputs to uncover errors that ordinary testing might miss.

Konstantopoulos said Tempo had also been patched, while Reth developers released version 2.10.0, Optimism published OP Reth v2.8.1, and Base issued version 1.5.3.

The Reth release classified the update as high priority for node operators, including those responsible for building blocks.

The coordinated response highlights a vulnerability in Ethereum's increasingly interconnected software ecosystem: multiple blockchain networks can inherit the same underlying defect when they rely on shared execution software.

However, Konstantopoulos said the affected code did not expose users of Base and other OP Stack networks to faulty withdrawals.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

He explained that these networks' withdrawal systems were not vulnerable to the error, while ecosystem bridges generally rely on transaction receipt roots or multisignature authorization rather than the affected state-root calculations.

He also apologized for the disruption, emphasizing Paradigm's responsibility for maintaining infrastructure used across the Ethereum ecosystem.

Base separately confirmed that the vulnerability had not affected its users, providing additional details about how its security systems prevented the error from threatening the network's integrity.

In a Nov. 5 status update, the Coinbase-backed network said it discovered the Reth issue on Nov. 4 and immediately patched its block builders.

The team also independently recalculated the blockchain's state root to verify its accuracy.

Base said its proof system uses a separate implementation to verify state roots, providing an additional check capable of detecting discrepancies in calculations produced by Reth.

“We've verified the current state root is correct and users were not affected.”

The version 1.5.3 release also addresses a separate operational consequence of the defect, preventing Base validators from halting when encountering invalid state roots.

Node operators were encouraged to upgrade, although Base said they would not need to resynchronize their nodes or take additional recovery steps.

Nevertheless, concerns about the software flaw prompted precautionary measures across parts of the decentralized finance ecosystem.

Frax Finance reported on Nov. 5 that cross-chain messaging protocol LayerZero had temporarily suspended certain transfer routes while developers assessed the situation.

Frax said its assets and smart contracts continued operating normally and that user funds remained safe.

The restrictions did not establish that LayerZero's bridge contracts were vulnerable to the Reth defect. Instead, they demonstrated how concerns about shared blockchain infrastructure can prompt other services to restrict activity while assessing operational risks.

There were no confirmed reports of funds being stolen through the state-root calculation flaw.

Konstantopoulos said the coordinated patching effort had secured Reth-based infrastructure, including systems that depend on blockchain state proofs.

However, the availability of corrected software does not mean every independently operated node has installed it.

The remaining priority is for infrastructure providers and node operators to deploy the patched releases, while services that restricted activity determine when they can resume normal operations.

#5294. Coinbase Says 99% of Customer Crypto Is Offline and Out of Hackers’ Reach

Coinbase Says 99% of Customer Crypto Is Offline and Out of Hackers’ Reach

Coinbase is moving to reassure customers that what happened at Binance can’t easily happen there.

In a blog post Wednesday, the U.S. exchange said it wasn’t affected by last week’s hack of Binance, in which attackers drained about $6.4 billion from the rival exchange’s hot wallets.

Coinbase said it keeps more than 99% of customer assets in cold storage, meaning offline wallets that can’t be reached over the internet. It moves funds into internet-connected hot wallets only as customers need them.

The Binance incident “has understandably left customers asking” how Coinbase guards against a similar attack, the post said.

Coinbase laid out several layers of protection. Private keys for its cold wallets are split into pieces and never fully reassembled, even when signing transactions, and no single employee has standing access to the hot-wallet signing service. Strict limits cap how fast funds can move from cold to hot wallets, and unusual withdrawal spikes are held until staff review them. The exchange can also trigger “kill switches” that take signing keys offline entirely.

The company said it assumes employees will be targeted by phishing, so its controls are designed so that a stolen password, session or device can’t be used on its own, and sensitive actions require multiple approvals.

That focus on insiders carries weight for Coinbase. In May 2025, it disclosed that criminals had bribed overseas customer support agents to steal personal data on less than 1% of its monthly transacting users, then demanded a $20 million ransom that Coinbase refused to pay.

Last week, Coinbase said a security incident at analytics vendor Amplitude exposed contact data for a “small subset” of customers, though funds weren’t affected.

Coinbase also said customer assets are held 1:1 and aren’t lent out unless customers direct it to, and it reported $8.6 billion in cash and cash equivalents and $377 billion in assets on its platform as of Sept. 30. It flagged artificial intelligence as a fast-changing threat and pledged further security investment.

The Binance theft, which the FBI has attributed to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group, has rattled the industry. Blockchain analytics firm Elliptic found that the laundering spanned about 12,000 wallets in under four days, while stablecoin issuers froze about 44% of the haul.

Separately, Brazil’s Mercado Bitcoin halted withdrawals after a $40 million hack, and French bank Crédit Mutuel Arkéa recently confirmed a cyberattack that led to a $133 million crypto theft.

#5292. Greece ends years of crypto tax uncertainty with new 10% levy on Bitcoin profits

Annual gains up to €500 are exempt under the approved bill, while directives on transparency and audits are still forthcoming.

Greece has approved a 10% cryptocurrency capital gains tax and a separate 15% levy on staking and decentralized finance (DeFi) income.

The legislation, passed by parliament on Nov. 5, establishes the country's first comprehensive framework for taxing digital assets, with the new rules scheduled to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

According to Reuters, annual cryptocurrency gains of up to €500 will be exempt, while investors exceeding that threshold will face taxation on their profits.

The framework also allows qualifying losses to be carried forward for five years to offset future gains.

Under the finance ministry's October proposal, staking, lending and DeFi liquidity rewards would attract a 15% tax as interest income, separating those earnings from trading profits.

Reuters reports a 10% capital-gains tax with annual gains up to €500 exempt; implementation directives are forthcoming.

The consultation proposed 10% on individuals' transfer gains, generally transfer price minus acquisition price.

The consultation proposed treating staking, lending and liquidity returns as interest at 15%.

Parliament's approval settles the headline framework, while the promised directives address transparency and audit rules.

The graphic does not establish commencement, filing deadlines or the operation of the exemption above €500. The panel describes an October proposal, not final enacted staking or transfer-calculation rules.

Qualitative milestone map, not a time scale or a probability forecast. The selectable panel contrasts activity classifications in the October 7 consultation proposal. No tax-liability calculation is made.

The ministry also proposed exempting crypto-to-crypto swaps from immediate taxation, although parliamentary concerns about the final wording leave their treatment unresolved.

Meanwhile, the legislation provides a 12-month window for investors to voluntarily declare cryptocurrency gains from previous years without late-filing penalties or interest, subject to specified conditions.

The measure comes as Greek authorities struggle to monitor cryptocurrency activity conducted through overseas platforms.

A senior finance ministry official reportedly said that the government could not estimate potential tax revenue because most domestic investors use foreign exchanges, making the market difficult to measure.

Further directives covering transparency requirements and tax audits are expected in the coming weeks.

Greece's new rate places it among Europe's lower-tax jurisdictions for cryptocurrency investors, even as several countries have increased taxes on digital asset profits.

According to a Nov. 6 analysis by CryptoDiffer, Cyprus taxes crypto gains at 8%, while Belgium and Bulgaria apply 10% rates and Croatia charges 12%.

Other European countries have moved in the opposite direction.

Italy increased its standard cryptocurrency capital-gains tax to 33% in 2026, while Romania raised its rate to 16%. Sweden imposes a 30% capital-gains tax on qualifying crypto profits.

However, some European jurisdictions offer investors exemptions based on how long they hold their assets.

CryptoDiffer identified Germany and Portugal as exempting qualifying cryptocurrency gains after one year of holding, while Luxembourg applies a six-month threshold. Croatia offers an exemption after two years and Czechia after three.

Switzerland, Slovenia and Malta were also identified as jurisdictions where qualifying private-investor crypto gains can be exempt from capital-gains tax.

These differences reflect Europe's fragmented approach to crypto taxation, with investors facing substantially different liabilities depending on their country, holding period and classification of investment activity.

#5291. $7.6 Trillion in October: Broadridge’s Distributed Ledger Repo Platform Hits Processing Record

Broadridge Financial Solutions has shared data on the use of its Distributed Ledger Repo (DLR) platform to execute and settle repurchase agreement (repo) transactions. In October 2026, $7.6 trillion in repo transactions were executed using the platform. This represents an average daily volume of $345 billion.

Repo transactions involve the temporary sale of securities with an agreement to repurchase them at a specified price. In practice, repos are a form of short-term borrowing, with the securities serving as collateral. They’re commonly used by financial institutions to raise cash and manage their funding needs.

Broadridge’s DLR platform uses a distributed ledger to execute and settle repo transactions. The company has also recently unveiled a new platform called DLX that can be used to issue, trade, settle, custody, and service tokenized assets throughout their lifecycles.

Broadridge global head of digital innovation Horacio Barakat noted that earlier implementations of blockchain in financial services focused on individual use cases, but now, for tokenized assets to be adopted by banks, broker-dealers, and asset managers, it’s important to think about how they can be implemented within existing workflows and infrastructure. Barakat expects to see more institutions do this in 2027.

It’s worth noting that the $7.6 trillion in repo transactions executed in October is the total notional value of repo transactions during the month. Repo transactions are constantly churning, with new transactions being executed to replace expiring ones.

This data therefore gives a sense of the level of activity in the securities financing market using Broadridge’s DLR platform but doesn’t provide insights into crypto market activity or investor appetite for Bitcoin and Ether.

It also doesn’t provide insights into the amount of new capital flowing into crypto.

To understand the extent to which Broadridge’s DLR platform provides benefits around faster transfer of collateral and settlement, it would be helpful to have data around settlement times and the flow of collateral. Nevertheless, the data does give a sense of the level of securities financing activity using the platform.

Long-awaited NU7 upgrade was finally activated on Zcash's mainnet at block 3,543,405 earlier this morning. The private cryptocurrency project became the first-ever to deploy long-term security mechanisms directly into the protocol, solving what some refer to as "Bitcoin's main dilemma": how to maintain the network after the emission zeroes out.

Matter of fact, the controversial Zcash Community Grant worth 50,000 ZEC is also a part of sustainability initiative.

Technically the network accelerated by 300% as the time for block production was cut from 75 to 25 seconds. To remain within the strict limit of 21 million ZEC, the rewards for mining were gradually cut too. Besides, NU7 upgrade blocks old type transactions making coins in legacy pools like Sprout unredeemable for the stability of code.

Zooko, who is Zooko Wilcox himself, a main man behind Zcash, greeted the upgrade in a laconic, yet eloquent manner, saying "Happy NU7 Everyone!". #5287. AI watchdog report indicates we may have less than 6 months before AI super intelligence arrives

The estimate covers well-specified tasks; METR's judgment that AI drives most of the acceleration rests partly on redacted evidence.

Anthropic's AI models were likely improving on tasks with clear success criteria roughly twice as fast in October 2026 as they did between March 2024 and October 2025, according to a Nov. 5 assessment by METR, an independent model-evaluation group.

METR judges that AI assistance probably accounts for most of the recent acceleration. But Anthropic redacted much of the evidence behind that judgment, leaving outsiders with a clearer view of the faster benchmark trend than of what caused it.

The central published measurement uses AECI, Anthropic's version of the Epoch Capabilities Index. METR estimated that AECI's fitted growth rate after October 2025 was 1.9 times its earlier rate, with a 95% confidence interval of 1.5 to 2.8 times. The analysis includes snapshots of unreleased models, so it covers more than the products customers could access.

METR interprets that trend as roughly two years of historical benchmark progress achieved in the past year. The 1.9-times fit is distinct from its broader judgment of roughly twice the historical pace on well-specified tasks. That judgment carries substantial uncertainty, including whether the same acceleration extends to broader work.

Those limits matter because success on clean, easily graded tasks may translate unevenly into real-world usefulness. METR also cautions that an unusually slow historical baseline could make the acceleration appear larger. In the other direction, model results arrive after training, potentially concealing a more recent change in research speed.

METR says it confidently ruled out an acceleration in the growth of training compute as the explanation for the faster progress. The detailed evidence supporting that finding was redacted.

Beyond that exclusion, separating causes was less decisive. METR says non-AI factors likely played a significant role in the acceleration in late 2025, while judging that AI assistance now accounts for a majority of it.

The distinction also leaves people at the center of the most important training work. METR says AI was not yet making highly significant, fully autonomous contributions to those parts of Anthropic's model-training process. The reported speedup primarily involved researchers using AI assistance.

The benchmark trend is reported; attributing most of the acceleration to AI remains METR's uncertain judgment.

A measured acceleration does not by itself establish what caused it.

AECI measures benchmark progress on well-specified tasks. The 1.9x fit is separate from METR's broader roughly 2x judgment. Attribution to AI is substantially uncertain, and the diagram does not quantify the shares of different causes.

Qualitative diagram of METR's retained textual findings. No publisher figure, chart-shape extraction, numerical geometry, original calculation or staff survey is used.

AECI measures benchmark progress on well-specified tasks. The 1.9x fit is separate from METR's broader roughly 2x judgment. Attribution to AI is substantially uncertain, and the diagram does not quantify the shares of different causes.

Anthropic withheld a majority of the evidence METR found most informative for its risk conclusions. The redactions covered detailed estimates of acceleration and AI's contribution at different training stages, intermediate capability measurements, algorithmic-progress estimates, R&D inputs, bottleneck analyses and forecasts. Some interview and AI-contribution evidence was published, leaving readers able to inspect only part of the case behind METR's judgment.

Anthropic co-founder Sam McCandlish broadly agreed that AI was speeding research, according to The Associated Press. AP reported that he acknowledged the redactions made METR's work harder to check, while defending them because the details were commercially sensitive and could help other developers accelerate.

METR's companion review of Anthropic's August Risk Report, also published Nov. 5, addresses models available on July 15. It questions the confidence of the public report's argument that an early-warning acceleration threshold had not been crossed. That threshold concerns AI-driven research acceleration as a warning signal, rather than proof that catastrophic risks have materialized.

Researchers at both organizations still leaned toward the threshold remaining uncrossed then, while METR considered a crossing plausible. METR also agreed that direct catastrophic risks from those July models were low.

The main assessment ran from Aug. 12 to Oct. 29 and was separate from the employee-like evaluator program Anthropic announced Oct. 15. For public scrutiny, the unresolved gap is specific: the faster benchmark trend is described, but much of the evidence dividing that progress between AI assistance and other causes remains confidential.

At the pace METR measured, six months could deliver roughly a year’s worth of progress on Anthropic’s benchmarks. The case for superintelligence within that window hinges on what the next models can do with those gains. If they can design training experiments, spot promising results, and help turn them into better models, each generation could shorten the time it takes to build the next.

For that to produce superintelligence within six months, the gains would have to carry over from tasks with clear answers to open-ended work where even experts have to figure out what to try next. The first sign might come from inside an AI lab, when a model runs an experiment its researchers hadn’t thought to try, and the result helps build a more capable successor.
